record.paper_title: (E,E′N) and (E,E′NN) Experiments at NIKHEF, Mainz and JLab and Open Problems in One- and Two-Nucleon Emissions
record.original_question: Can recoil-polarization measurements in exclusive (e,e′pp) and (e,e′pn) reactions, combined with resolution of specific residual-nucleus final states, provide a practical way to separate correlation-driven knockout from processes generated by two-body currents and thereby determine the full scattering amplitudes more completely? The open problem is whether polarization observables add enough independent information to cleanly decompose the competing reaction mechanisms in two-nucleon emission.

evidence.quote: Experimentally, additional and precise information will come from measurement of the recoil polarization of the ejected proton in either (e,e′pp) or (e,e′pn).
Resolving different final states is a precise filter to disentangle and separately investigate the different processes due to correlations and/or two-body currents.
Ultimately, a complete determination of the scattering amplitudes is only possible with polarization measurements.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider exclusive electron-induced two-nucleon knockout reactions on a nuclear target, in which an incoming electron with four-momentum k scatters to a final electron with four-momentum k', exchanging a virtual photon of four-momentum q = k - k', and two outgoing nucleons (either a pp pair or a pn pair) are detected in coincidence while the residual (A-2)-nucleus is left in a specific discrete final state f. The differential cross section for such an (e,e'NN) reaction can be decomposed in terms of hadronic response functions that depend on bilinear combinations of the transition amplitudes M_{fi} between the initial nuclear ground state and the chosen residual state, mediated by (i) one-body currents acting on correlated nucleon pairs arising from short-range and tensor correlations in the nuclear wave function, and (ii) explicit two-body meson-exchange and isobar currents (including pion exchange and intermediate Δ excitation). In addition to unpolarized cross sections, one may consider polarization observables, defined as follows: the recoil polarization P = (P_L, P_T, P_N) of one of the ejected nucleons (longitudinal, transverse in the scattering plane, and normal to it) measured with unpolarized beam and target, and the polarization-transfer coefficients P'_i obtained with a longitudinally polarized electron beam. Each such observable is a specific bilinear function of the amplitudes M_{fi}.

Question: Do the recoil-polarization observables of one outgoing nucleon in (e,e'pp) and (e,e'pn) reactions, taken together with the experimental resolution of individual residual-nucleus final states f, supply sufficiently many independent bilinear functionals of the amplitudes M_{fi} to (a) cleanly decompose the cross section into contributions originating from nucleon-nucleon correlations versus contributions from two-body currents (including Δ-isobar excitation), and (b) achieve a complete determination of all independent complex scattering amplitudes M_{fi} (up to an overall phase) for the chosen final state?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that (e,e'NN) experiments have continued at facilities such as Mainz and JLab, and theoretical frameworks for polarization observables in two-nucleon knockout have been developed, but a definitive experimental demonstration that recoil-polarization observables suffice to fully disentangle correlation and two-body-current mechanisms and to completely determine the scattering amplitudes has not been reported. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Electroinduced two-nucleon knockout reactions
status_evidence.snippet: Polarization measurements proposed as a means to fully determine the scattering amplitudes in (e,e'NN).
status_evidence.claim: Identified as an open problem within the field of two-nucleon emission studies.
